the postoperative serum of high-risk breast cancer patients may be analysed by anion-exchange followed by SELDI MS to search for novel prognostic markers.
postoperative serum protein profiles may predict recurrence free survival in patients with high risk primary breast cancer.
postoperative serum proteomic profiling may predict recurrence-free breast cancer survival, and that this approach may improve selection of high-risk primary cancer patients for adjuvants therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of prognostic markers in serum of patients with breast cancer.
the development of a novel prognostic test for breast cancer patients, based on a postoperative serum protein profile.

the development of new serum-based prognostic tools for breast cancer patients, which may improve the selection of high-risk patients for adjuvancy therapy, and thereby reduce overtreatment of low-risk patients, and under-treatment of high-risk patients.

the presented data warrant further research, and that the presented results are promising.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the postoperative serum protein profile of high-risk primary BC patients may be a useful tool for predicting the individual risk of recurrence, and thereby for improving the selection of patients for postoperative adjuvant therapy.
we have demonstrated the value of a proteomic approach to the discovery of new prognostic factors, but that the clinical value of the markers discovered in this study remains to be determined.
the postoperative serum peptide profile may be useful for prognostic purposes, and that further studies are warranted to validate these findings.

the postoperative serum of breast cancer patients contains information that may aid in the prediction of disease outcome.
the postoperative serum protein profile may provide additional prognostic information, and that this information is not redundant to that obtained from clinical and pathological parameters.
postoperative serum proteomics may be a useful tool in breast cancer prognostics.
